description:
=== DONE (s473t5e) ===

FOUND s473t5e (#1501 round 6, `re/` CHECK 1) as the cause of the recovery line
three files share in `baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv`:

    aborted-forms:2: end of file on #<dynamic-extent string-input-stream
    (unavailable) from ";;; pcl:...">

  t/re/alpha_assertions.t   1784/74   421 rows short
  t/re/regexp_normal.t      1850/8    311 rows short
  t/re/regex_sets_compat.t  1600/258  311 rows short

All three are two-line drivers that `do './t/re/regexp.t'`, which drives
`t/re/re_tests`: for every row it runs `$subject = eval qq("$subject"); die $@
if $@;`.  re_tests line 1859 is

    /^\D{11}/a<TAB>\x{10FFFF}\x{10FFFF}...(ten of them)<TAB>n<TAB>-<TAB>-

and PCL's emission for `"\x{10FFFF}"` is a CL string literal holding the
character RAW (`Pl::ExprToCL::_cl_string_literal_form` splits out only
surrogates, U+FFFE/U+FFFF and >U+10FFFF).  All three files stopped at exactly
test 1858, which is that line.

THE CAUSE IS THE TRANSPORT, NOT THE EMITTER.  `pl2cl`'s transpile-server
protocol (`_run_server`) is char-counted --

    Request:  <pkg>\n<captures>\n<features>\n<deps>\n<char-count>\n<code>
    Response: ok\n<char-count>\n<cl-code>

-- and the layer was `:encoding(utf-8)`, the STRICT encoding.  perl calls the
2,048 surrogates, U+FDD0-U+FDEF and every plane's last two code points
NON-CHARACTERS, refuses to encode them, and substitutes the `\x{...}` ESCAPE
TEXT.  Measured, both directions:

    cp       layer              chars in   bytes   chars back  first back-ord
    10FFFF   :encoding(utf-8)   3          12      12          5C  (a `\`)
    10FFFF   :utf8              3          6       3           10FFFF
    D800     :encoding(utf-8)   3          10      10          5C
    FDD0     :encoding(utf-8)   3          14      14          5C
    1F600    :encoding(utf-8)   3          6       3           1F600  (fine)

The count then no longer describes the bytes: the reader on the other side
stops short, and what it got is a TRUNCATED form -- an unterminated string,
i.e. `end of file on #<string-input-stream ... from ";;; pcl:...">` from
`p-eval`'s own `(with-input-from-string (in cl-text) (read in ...))`.
`p-eval` catches it into `$@`, `do` returns undef, and regexp.t's `do $file
or die $@` kills the whole file: two aborted top-level forms, exactly as the
`sig` column says.

THE EXACT SET perl's strict layer refuses, probed: 70 code points sampled --
D800 DBFF-DC00 DFFF (the whole surrogate block) FDD0-FDEF FFFE-FFFF
1FFFE-1FFFF ... 10FFFE-10FFFF.

FIX: `_run_server` uses `:utf8`, the PERMISSIVE layer -- which is the one
`pl2cl`'s OWN STDOUT/STDERR already use for the file-mode emission (line 361,
"Output UTF-8 so non-ASCII chars ... are valid for SBCL's reader"), and which
SBCL's `:external-format :utf-8` on the pipe reads and writes byte for byte.
Two transports of ONE emission that disagreed, and the file-mode spelling was
the right one (CLAUDE.md rule 11).  ONE line each way.

MEASURED after the fix: all 66 non-surrogate code points cross intact in both
directions (`eval qq("\x{10FFFF}")` gives length 1 / ord 1114111, as perl).

RESIDUE #1712: a SURROGATE in the eval's own SOURCE still fails, because
SBCL's `:utf-8` external format refuses to ENCODE one onto the pipe.

OPERATIONAL FINDING: a desynchronised request can produce a syntactically
VALID but wrong transpile, and the eval DISK cache under
`~/.pcl-cache/evals/` then makes it permanent.  One such entry was found on
this box and removed by hand:

    ~/.pcl-cache/evals/e2bff49efedb66cf02c54ac30cfa2929.lisp
      (p-length (p-unparsable-quote "q{mai"))

With the layer fixed the desync cannot recur except through #1712, but a
machine that ran the old code keeps its poisoned entries until they prune
(30 days) -- and while one is present the affected eval is SILENTLY WRONG,
not loud.  If a future session sees an inexplicable `q{...` or
`p-unparsable-quote` in an eval, grep the evals cache before probing.

GUARD: `Pl/t/wide-codepoint-01.t` rows 12 + 13 (11 -> 13 rows; that file
already owns the high-code-point emission path).  Both rows FAIL on a
`git archive ee53ce76` extraction with a fresh module cache.
subject: DONE (s473t5e): the pl2cl transpile server's STRICT `:encoding(utf-8)` layer substituted the `\x{...}` escape text for perl's non-characters, desynchronising the char-counted protocol -- `eval "\x{10FFFF}"` died `end of file on string-input-stream` and cost three t/re/ files 1,043 rows
